title: The Shawshank Redemption
description: A banker sentenced to life for a murder he says he didn't commit forms a lasting friendship in prison while quietly planning his escape.
facts: It is based on Stephen King's 1982 novella 'Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption'.
Frank Darabont wrote and directed it, and reportedly bought the film rights from King for $5,000.
It earned only about $16 million at the US box office during its original 1994 run.
It received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, but won none.
Most prison scenes were shot at the Ohio State Reformatory in Mansfield, Ohio.
In King's novella, Red is an Irishman; in the film he is played by Morgan Freeman.
Tom Hanks was reportedly among the actors considered for the role of Andy Dufresne.
The posters Andy uses to hide his tunnel feature Rita Hayworth, Marilyn Monroe and Raquel Welch.
The film found its big audience later, through video rentals and repeated TV broadcasts.
It has spent years at or near the top of IMDb's Top 250 list.

title: Inception
description: A thief who steals secrets from people's dreams is offered a chance to erase his past by planting an idea in a target's mind.
facts: Christopher Nolan spent about ten years developing the idea before the film was made.
It won four Oscars: Cinematography, Sound Editing, Sound Mixing and Visual Effects.
The spinning hallway fight was filmed on a real rotating set, not mainly with digital effects.
Hans Zimmer built the score around a slowed-down piece of Edith Piaf's 'Non, je ne regrette rien'.
Its deep, blaring horn sound was widely copied in movie trailers for years afterwards.
Filming took place in six countries: Japan, the UK, France, Morocco, Canada and the US.
It cost around $160 million to make and grossed more than $800 million worldwide.
Marion Cotillard had already won the Best Actress Oscar for La Vie en Rose before joining the cast.
The film's tagline was 'Your mind is the scene of the crime'.
The famous ending cuts to black while the spinning top is still wobbling, and Nolan left it open on purpose.

facts.title: The Godfather
facts.description: The aging head of a New York crime family hands control to his reluctant youngest son.
facts: It is based on Mario Puzo's 1969 novel, and Puzo co-wrote the screenplay with director Francis Ford Coppola.
Paramount executives reportedly considered replacing Coppola during production.
It won three Oscars: Best Picture, Best Actor for Marlon Brando and Best Adapted Screenplay.
Brando refused his Best Actor Oscar and sent Sacheen Littlefeather to decline it on his behalf.
The cat Brando holds in the opening scene was a stray found on the set, and the moment was improvised.
Nino Rota's score was disqualified from an Oscar nomination because he had reused music from an earlier film.
The studio was reluctant to cast Al Pacino as Michael Corleone, but Coppola insisted on him.
It was made on a budget of roughly $6 million and earned more than $240 million worldwide.
It was released in the United States in March 1972.
Its sequel, The Godfather Part II, also won the Oscar for Best Picture.

facts.title: The Dark Knight
facts.description: Batman faces the Joker, an anarchic criminal who pushes Gotham City to its breaking point.
facts: Christopher Nolan directed it as the sequel to Batman Begins.
Heath Ledger won a posthumous Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for playing the Joker.
Several sequences were shot with IMAX cameras, a first for a major narrative feature film.
The truck flip through the Chicago streets was filmed for real rather than created digitally.
Chicago stands in for Gotham City, and the film also shot scenes in Hong Kong.
Ledger reportedly kept a diary in character while preparing for the Joker role.
It grossed more than $1 billion worldwide.
The hospital explosion was filmed by demolishing a real, former candy factory in Chicago.
Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard composed the score together.
It won two Oscars: Best Supporting Actor and Best Sound Editing.

facts.title: Pulp Fiction
facts.description: The lives of two hitmen, a boxer, a gangster and his wife intertwine in separate, out-of-order stories.
facts: Quentin Tarantino directed it, and Roger Avary shares a story credit.
It won the Palme d'Or at the 1994 Cannes Film Festival.
It won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.
It revived John Travolta's career and earned him a Best Actor nomination.
The film tells three interwoven stories out of chronological order.
It had a budget of about $8 million and earned over $200 million worldwide.
The glowing contents of the mysterious briefcase are never revealed.
The twist contest at Jack Rabbit Slim's became one of the most imitated dance scenes in film.
The Bible verse Jules recites is largely an invention that Tarantino adapted from a Japanese film.
Its soundtrack features surf rock, including Dick Dale's 'Misirlou' over the opening credits.
